title: Hijacking of Aircraft and Protection of Aircraft and International Airports (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Hijacking of Aircraft and Protection of Aircraft and International Airports (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Acceding to Beijing aviation treaties
sections.summary: Singapore intends to accede to the Beijing Convention 2010 and Beijing Protocol 2010 to strengthen defence against terrorist attacks, especially against civil aviation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In our ongoing efforts to further strengthen our defence against such terrorist attacks, especially against civil aviation corporations, we intend to accede to two international aviation security treaties: the Convention on the Suppression of Unlawful Acts Relating to International Civil Aviation, also known as the Beijing Convention 2010, and the Protocol Supplementary to the Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft, also known as the Beijing Protocol 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Due to the cross-border nature of the threat, international cooperation is necessary to combat such threats; two, the Beijing Convention 2010 and Beijing Protocol 2010 will strengthen Singapore's ability to deal with terrorism-related threats to the safety and security of civil aviation; three, the two Beijing treaties will enable us to better protect Singaporeans, by providing a clear basis for us to exercise our criminal jurisdiction as provided for under the two treaties; and four, the Beijing Convention 2010 and Beijing Protocol 2010 will also facilitate the extradition of offenders and provision of mutual legal assistance.

sections.label: Acts criminalised by Beijing Convention
sections.summary: The Beijing Convention criminalises using aircraft to cause death or damage, releasing BCN weapons, transporting such substances, and cyber attacks on air navigation facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In addition to those already criminalised under the two Montreal treaties, the Beijing Convention criminalises the following acts: one, using an aircraft for the purpose of causing death, serious bodily injury or serious damage; two, releasing or discharging from an aircraft, or using on board or against aircraft any biological, chemical or nuclear (BCN) weapons or explosive, radioactive or similar substances; three, transporting, causing to be transported, or facilitating the transport of BCN weapons or explosive, radioactive or similar substances, and so on, on board an aircraft; and four, cyber attacks on air navigation facilities.

sections.label: Amendment Bill gives effect to treaties
sections.summary: The Hijacking of Aircraft and Protection of Aircraft and International Airports (Amendment) Bill will give effect to the Beijing treaties and facilitate Singapore's implementation of treaty obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Hijacking of Aircraft and Protection of Aircraft and International Airports (Amendment) Bill will give effect to the Beijing treaties and facilitate Singapore's implementation of the obligations under these treaties when we accede to them.

sections.label: Hijacking offence for aircraft in service
sections.summary: With the amendment, the offence of hijacking can also be committed in relation to an aircraft in service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: With the amendment, the offence of hijacking can also be committed in relation to an aircraft in service.

sections.label: New section 5A on aircraft use
sections.summary: The new section 5A criminalises the use of an aircraft in service for the purpose of causing death, serious bodily injury, or serious damage to property or the environment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The new section 5A criminalises the use of an aircraft in service for the purpose of causing death, serious bodily injury, or serious damage to property or the environment.

sections.label: New section 9 stipulates penalties
sections.summary: The new section 9 stipulates the penalties for the various offences under the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The new section 9 stipulates the penalties for the various offences under the Act.

sections.label: Extradition, legal assistance, aviation offences
sections.summary: New sections extend extradition and mutual legal assistance to new offences, allow Beijing treaties as extradition basis, and criminalise dangerous aviation actions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The new section 11 to extend the provisions relating to extradition under the Act and the Extradition Act to the new offences inserted by the Bill, and provides that the Beijing treaties and their predecessor treaties may be used as the legal basis for extradition in the absence of an extradition treaty.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The new section 12 provides that in the provision of mutual legal assistance to any state which is a party to the Convention for a criminal matter involving an offence in that state corresponding to a relevant offence, that offence in the state will be deemed not to be an offence of a political character.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to criminalise certain dangerous actions relating to aviation, including the use of aircraft as a weapon.

sections.label: ICAO Technical Instructions court guidance
sections.summary: Asks if the Minister can share whether and how courts should consider ICAO's Technical Instructions when interpreting the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, to provide guidance to airlines in navigating the implementation of this Bill, can the Minister share if and how the ICAO's Technical Instructions should be considered by the Courts in Singapore in the interpretation of this Bill?

sections.label: Airline cargo process review
sections.summary: Asks if the Government has worked with the airline industry to review cargo processes so airlines avoid criminal liability under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister share if the Government has worked with the airline industry to ensure proper review of their cargo processes so that airlines do not inadvertently expose themselves to criminal liability under the Bill?

sections.label: Beijing Convention and Protocol accession
sections.summary: The Bill paves the way for Singapore's accession to the Beijing Convention and Protocol 2010, which criminalise using civil aircraft as weapons and transporting dangerous materials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Hijacking of Aircraft and Protection of Aircraft and International Airports Amendment Bill will pave the way for Singapore's accession to the Beijing Convention 2010 and Beijing Protocol 2010.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In summary, the Convention criminalises the use of civil aircraft as a weapon and the illegal transport or discharge of dangerous materials, including explosive, radioactive, biological, chemical or nuclear (BCN) weapons to attack aircraft or other targets.

sections.label: Signatories to Convention and Protocol
sections.summary: Asks how many other countries are signatories to the Convention and Protocol.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, I would like to ask how many other countries are signatories to the Convention and Protocol.

sections.label: Aviation cybersecurity breaches reported
sections.summary: States Eurocontrol reported at least 1,260 cybersecurity breaches against airlines and aviation bodies in 2020, and Singapore Airlines suffered a data breach last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to Eurocontrol, at least 1,260 cybersecurity breaches against airlines and other aviation bodies were reported in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore Airlines also suffered from a data breach.

sections.label: Penalties for offences under Act
sections.summary: Section 9 of the Act lists penalties of life imprisonment or a fine not exceeding $1 million for offences under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Section 9 of the Act lists the penalties for offences under the Act, namely, life imprisonment or a fine not exceeding $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Do these penalties apply if the offender was successful in their attempt and caused death and destruction?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would capital punishment be more appropriate to match the severity of the crime?

sections.label: Hijacking offence and domestic terrorism
sections.summary: Amended section 3(1) defines hijacking by force, threats or technological means, potentially covering malicious hackers taking control of aircraft.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, domestic terrorism is well on the way to become a much bigger threat than before, as widening disparities and misinformation threaten the unity of a nation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill is thus important to ensure that our laws are relevant, comprehensive and in time for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The amended section 3(1) provides that "a person who unlawfully and intentionally seizes or exercises control of an aircraft in service by the use of force or by threats of any kind, or by any technological means, commits the offence of hijacking, whatever his nationality or citizenship, whatever the state in which the aircraft is registered and whether the aircraft is in Singapore or elsewhere." Depending on the facts and circumstances, this provision could potentially cover acts by malicious hackers to take control of an aircraft by hacking into the aircraft systems.

sections.label: Drone collision with aircraft
sections.summary: Flying a drone to intentionally collide with a landing aircraft may fall under section 5(1)(a) of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For example, depending on the circumstances, the flying of a drone to intentionally collide with a landing aircraft may potentially fall under the scope of section 5(1)(a) of the Act, which covers acts, regardless of the means used, which damage an aircraft so as to render it incapable of flight or as to be likely to endanger its safety in flight.

sections.label: Hijacking offence application to aircraft
sections.summary: Under amended section 3, hijacking applies if the person is a Singapore citizen, the act is in or over Singapore, or the aircraft is used in Singapore's military, customs or Police service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: For example, under the amended section 3, the offence of hijacking can be applied to such aircraft if (a) the person seizing or exercising control of the aircraft is a citizen of Singapore; (b) his act is committed in or over Singapore; or (c) the aircraft is used in Singapore's military, customs or Police service.

sections.label: ICAO Technical Instructions for dangerous materials
sections.summary: The Technical Instructions are published by ICAO to ensure dangerous materials undergo necessary acceptance, packaging, documentation and loading processes for safe air transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Technical Instructions are published by ICAO to ensure that dangerous materials are subjected to the necessary acceptance, packaging, documentation and loading processes for safe transport by air.

sections.label: Singapore cargo screening regime
sections.summary: Singapore implements a rigorous cargo screening regime that is compliant with international standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Singapore also implements a rigorous cargo screening regime that is compliant with international standards.

sections.label: Bill international cooperation prosecution
sections.summary: The Bill's provisions would enhance these measures through international cooperation, including allowing Singapore to prosecute such individuals once apprehended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: With the provisions of this Bill, the effectiveness of these measures would be enhanced further through international cooperation, including allowing Singapore to prosecute such individuals once they are apprehended.
